title: Director, Global Regulatory Reporting, Core Compliance
description: About Invesco As one of the world’s leading independent global investment firms, Invesco is dedicated to rethinking possibilities for our clients. By delivering the combined power of our distinctive investment management capabilities, we provide a wide range of investment strategies and vehicles to our clients around the world. If you're looking for challenging work, intelligent colleagues, and exposure across a global footprint, come explore your potential at Invesco. What’s in it for you? Our people are at the ver y core of our success. Invesco employees get more out of life through our comprehensive compensation and benefit offerings including: Flexible paid time off Hybrid work schedule 401(K) matching of 100% up to the first 6% with a discretionary supplemental contribution Health & wellbeing benefits Parental Leave benefits Employee stock purchase plan Job Description The Team Global Regulatory Reporting (GRR) is part of Global Core Compliance and runs Invesco's global regulatory reporting framework. Our globally distributed team of people managers and individual contributors monitors, prepares, reviews, files, and escalates regulatory reports across regions and reporting regimes. A key focus is the global shareholder disclosure program, covering substantial shareholder, beneficial ownership, short-position, and takeover obligations, alongside Form PF and NFA filings. We work closely with Legal, Compliance, Technology, Operations, Data, Risk, Audit, and external vendors. Together we strengthen controls and deliver accurate, timely, technology-enabled reporting. The Rol e The Director, Global Regulatory Reporting is a strategic leadership role accountable for overseeing, delivering, and continuously improving Invesco's global regulatory reporting program. You will lead multiple related teams, including people managers. You will set priorities, allocate resources, and develop the plans and policies that drive team performance and results. You will resolve complex, multi-dimensional regulatory, data, and operational issues. You will also turn evolving requirements into scalable operating models and technology-enabled solutions. You will influence senior executives, vendors, and regulators to support the global Compliance program and the firm's strategic priorities. Key responsibilities: Leading and developing a global team of people managers and individual contributors. This includes setting direction, priorities, resourcing, backup coverage, and succession plans, and holding teams accountable for quality and timeliness. Owning the global shareholder disclosure program (substantial shareholder, beneficial ownership, short-position, and takeover filings). You will ensure filings are complete, accurate, timely, and well evidenced. Overseeing the preparation, review, and submission of Form PF and NFA filings, including CPO-PQR and CTA-PR. Providing senior guidance on regulatory interpretation and implementing new requirements with Legal and regional Compliance. You will also lead regulatory engagement on incidents, examinations, and remediation. Maintaining a risk-based control framework covering quality assurance, testing, and issue management. You will promptly escalate material exposures, control failures, and recurring issues. Partnering with Data Management, Technology, and external vendors to define requirements, resolve data issues, and oversee regulatory monitoring systems. Driving regulatory-change, remediation, automation, and responsibly governed AI-enabled initiatives with disciplined project governance. Influencing senior stakeholders, representing GRR in governance forums and firm-wide strategic initiatives, and fostering an inclusive, accountable, high-performing culture. Experience required: 10+ years of experience in investment management, financial services, regulatory reporting, Compliance, Legal, Operations, or a related control function. This includes substantial experience leading global or remote teams and people managers. Deep working knowledge of global shareholder disclosure regimes, including substantial shareholder, beneficial ownership, short-position, takeover, aggregation, attribution, and threshold-monitoring requirements across major jurisdictions. Proven experience overseeing recurring filings, complex reviews, control design, issue escalation, regulator or audit responses, and remediation in a deadline-driven environment. Strong understanding of asset-management processes, funds and accounts, position and transaction data, and regulatory reporting systems, data flows, and lineage. Experience partnering with technology teams and external vendors. This includes translating regulatory needs into clear business, data, control, and testing requirements, and implementing automation while keeping appropriate human oversight. title: Senior Compliance Officer – Enterprise FinCEN Programs Governance SME
description: Location: 4910 Tiedeman Road, Brooklyn Ohio Job Summary The Senior Compliance Officer serves as Financial Crimes Risk Management’s (FCRM) enterprise subject matter expert (SME) and senior second-line compliance authority for technical compliance with and meeting the spirit of FinCEN Programs such as Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs), Currency Transaction Reports (CTRs, including Purchase and Sale of Certain Monetary Instruments Recordkeeping aka Monetary Instrument Log [MIL]), Reports of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (FBARs), “Special Measures” Pursuant to Section 311 of the USA PATRIOT Act (Special Measures), and “Information Sharing” Pursuant to Section 314(a) and (b) of the USA PATRIOT Act (Information Sharing). This role provides enterprise-wide governance, oversight, credible challenge, and strategic guidance to help ensure related processes, procedures, standards, controls, systems, data, and supporting documentation are appropriately designed, implemented, maintained, and operating effectively. The Senior Compliance Officer partners across the first, second, and third lines of defense to identify regulatory risk, assess related control coverage and design, resolve complex matters, drive sustainable remediation, and promote consistent execution across all applicable legal entities, businesses, products, channels, and customer segments. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Serve as the enterprise subject matter expert for and to ensure technical compliance with and meeting the spirit of FinCEN Programs including SARs, CTRs / MIL, FBARs, Special Measures, Information Sharing, and related regulatory requirements and industry practices. Execute risk oversight activities in accordance with the FCRM governance framework, related standards, and requirements. Know and provide compliance oversight of technology evolution / transformation, data governance, data lineage / flows, data quality, data dependencies, data access, data platforms, record retention, system functionality, automated decisioning, rules, models, and other technology changes affecting SARs, CTRs / MIL, FBARs, Special Measures, and Information Sharing. Learn and identify the entire cradle-to-grave processes at KeyBank for SARs, CTRs / MIL, FBARs, Special Measures, and Information Sharing, including all technology inputs and/or manual processes which could affect outputs, to ensure full compliance with FinCEN Programs. Provide second-line oversight and credible challenge of all enterprise-wide processes, procedures, controls, systems, tools, data, and operational practices and facets supporting FinCEN Programs including SARs, CTRs / MIL, FBARs, Special Measures, and Information Sharing. Interpret applicable laws, rules, regulatory guidance, examination expectations, and enforcement themes; assess enterprise impact; and translate requirements into clear policies, standards, control expectations, and implementation guidance. Own and provide authoritative review and approval of enterprise policies and standards for FinCEN Programs including SARs, CTRs / MIL, FBARs, Special Measures, and Information Sharing, and oversee the governance of supporting first-line procedures and job aids. Evaluate whether controls are appropriately designed to mitigate inherent and residual risks and whether control execution is effective, consistent, evidenced, and sustainable across the enterprise. Identify gaps, emerging risks, inconsistent practices, control weaknesses, and potential regulatory exposure; communicate the risk clearly; and require timely corrective action or formal risk acceptance, as appropriate. Support enterprise risk assessments, including BSA/AML risk assessments, regulatory compliance risk assessments, risk and control self-assessments, customer risk methodologies, and topical assessments related to SARs, CTRs / MIL, FBARs, Special Measures, and Information Sharing. Define and monitor risk appetite, risk tolerance, key risk indicators, key performance indicators, control metrics, quality results, exceptions, backlogs, aging, and other management information used to assess program health. Review and challenge business process risk identification, new or modified products and services, customer journeys, delivery channels, acquisitions, integrations, third-party arrangements, and material changes that may affect SARs, CTRs / MIL, FBARs, Special Measures, and Information Sharing obligations. Provide senior compliance guidance and influence on complex, high-risk, novel, or escalated customer matters, including for SARs, CTRs / MIL, FBARs, Special Measures, and Information Sharing. Partner with Legal, BSA/AML leadership, FCRM teams, business compliance, operations, technology, data, model risk, fraud, privacy, third-party risk, Internal Audit, and independent testing teams to promote an integrated and consistent control environment. title: Manager, Technical Accounting and Equity Reporting
description: Our mission at ŌURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles. Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.  As Oura scales and prepares for life as a public company, equity compensation and non-routine technical accounting questions are becoming larger and more complex. We’re looking for a Manager, Technical Accounting and Equity Reporting to own stock-based compensation accounting and equity reporting end to end, and to serve as a technical accounting resource on complex and non-recurring transactions.You’ll own ASC 718 accounting and the equity roll-forwards, reconciliations, footnotes, and disclosures that flow from it; work through the accounting for share repurchases; document accounting positions in clear memos; and build SOX-ready processes and controls. You’ll partner closely with Legal, Stock Administration, Payroll, Tax, Corporate Finance, FP&A, Business Systems, and our external auditors. What You Will Do: Stock-based compensation accounting (ASC 718) Own the monthly stock-based compensation close: validate grant, vesting, forfeiture, and termination data, calculate and record expense by function, and prepare the related journal entries. Review valuation inputs and assumptions (e.g., Black-Scholes, 409A) with valuation specialists and support the related audit evidence. Account for modifications, cancellations, repurchases, and settlement mechanics, including net share settlement. Reconcile the cap table and equity administration platform to the general ledger, and resolve differences promptly.   Equity reporting and disclosures Prepare and review equity roll-forwards, APIC and stockholders’ equity activity, and stock-based compensation disclosures for quarterly and annual financial statements. Maintain audit-ready support and tie-outs for every equity figure in the financial statements and disclosures.   Liquidity events and capital structure Lead the accounting analysis for tender offers, secondary transactions, IPO-related events, and corporate reorganizations as they affect employee equity. Lead the modeling process around the expected financial statement impact of an IPO on equity awards, including expense recognition, net settlement, and tax withholding, and keep the model current as timing and terms evolve.   Technical accounting and policy Research complex accounting questions under US GAAP and write clear, well-supported technical memos that document facts, guidance, analysis, and conclusions. Serve as a technical resource on non-routine transactions beyond equity, as needed - areas could include: debt vs. equity accounting (ASC 480), debt (ASC 470), leases (ASC 842), business combinations (ASC 805), and global entity matters. Assist with drafting, updating, and maintaining accounting policies, and monitor new standards and SEC guidance for their impact on Oura.   Controls and audit Design, document, and operate key controls over equity and technical accounting in partnership with the SOX team, and remediate gaps promptly. Serve as a primary contact for external auditors on equity and technical accounting, including walkthroughs, PBC requests, and technical discussions. What you'll bring 6+ years of progressive accounting and financial reporting experience, including Big 4 or national firm experience. Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance; active CPA strongly preferred. Hands-on expertise in ASC 718, including options, RSUs, performance-condition awards, modifications, repurchases and tender offers. Strong working knowledge of US GAAP and SEC reporting, with experience in ASC 718. Experience producing equity roll-forwards, footnotes, and disclosures for audited financial statements, and reconciling an equity administration platform (e.g., Carta, Shareworks) to the general ledger. Demonstrated ability to research complex technical matters independently and write defensible accounting memos. Experience designing and operating SOX or other internal controls over financial reporting. Clear written and verbal communication, including explaining complex topics to non-accounting partners, and a record of mentoring or managing others. Nice to have: Public company or IPO-readiness experience. Workiva and Shareworks experience. Experience in consumer hardware, health technology, or subscription businesses.
